judged_text: The attendee-createMany and the downstream calendar/email side effects run non-atomically: prisma.booking.update commits new attendee rows before eventManager.updateCalendarAttendieves and sendAddGuestsEmails execute, with no transaction and no compensating delete. When updateCalendarAttendees throws (bad credential, calendar API failure) the handler rejects with a 500 but the guest rows are already persisted — bookings show guests who were never added to the external calendar event or emailed, and there is no remove-guests endpoint to undo them, so the data drift is permanent without manual SQL.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuestsHandler` the DB write happens first via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` and is committed before the external side effects (`await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` and then `sendAddGuestsEmails`). There is no `prisma.$transaction` wrapping these steps and no compensating rollback/delete if `updateCalendarAttendees` throws. Since `updateCalendarAttendees` is awaited outside any try/catch, a failure will reject the handler (500) after guests are already persisted, leaving the booking showing added guests even though calendar update (and potentially emails) did not complete.
